**Short answer:**  
An internship *can* provide a visa, but the employer must sponsor the appropriate work pass—**you cannot intern on a tourist visa or a Student’s Pass alone.**

---

### Singapore work passes for interns

| Pass | Who it’s for | Key rules |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| **Training Employment Pass (TEP)** | Degree/diploma holders earning **≥ S$3,000/month** | Employer applies; max 3 months (non-renewable). |
| **Work Holiday Programme (WHP)** | Students/graduates **18–25** from approved countries (e.g., Australia, France, Germany, HK, Japan, NZ, UK, US, etc.) | Self-applied via MOM; 6 months; no minimum salary. |
| **Training Work Permit (TWP)** | Semi-skilled trainees from approved sources | Sector-specific; employer applies; up to 6 months. |
| **Student’s Pass + ICA approval** | Full-time students at **approved Singapore institutions** doing *mandatory* curricular internships | School submits “Letter of Consent” to ICA; unpaid or stipend-only roles allowed. |

> **Most common for international university students:** TEP (paid roles ≥ S$3k) or WHP (if your country qualifies).  
> **Unpaid/low-stipend roles** usually require the curricular-internship route through your school.

---

### What to ask the employer
1. “Which work pass will you apply for?”  
2. “Is the monthly allowance ≥ S$3,000 (for TEP)?”  
3. “Will you cover the application fee and medical exam?”  
4. “Can you share the MOM/In-Principle Approval letter before I book flights?”

---

### Red flags
- “Work on a tourist visa / visa-free entry.” ❌ Illegal.  
- “We’ll figure out the pass after you arrive.” ❌ High risk.  
- No written offer stating the pass type and salary.

---

### Quick checklist for you
- [ ] Confirm your nationality’s WHP eligibility ([MOM WHP page](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-holiday-pass)).  
- [ ] Verify the internship is **paid ≥ S$3k** if you need a TEP.  
- [ ] Get the offer letter **before** applying for any pass.  
- [ ] Keep your university’s career centre in the loop—they often have pre-approved employer lists and can issue consent letters.
